title: Why Chips Matter: Semiconductors

endcard.line: Pictures: Rob Bulmahn (CC BY 2.0); Purdue Engineering (CC BY 4.0)

segments.say: Your phone, a car, a satellite, a power grid. All of them run on chips no bigger than a fingernail.

anim.title: A chip
items: Made on a thin disc of pure silicon
Each switch: on or off, one or zero

segments.say: A chip is built on a thin disc of very pure silicon. On it are billions of tiny switches, called transistors. Each one is on or off: a one or a zero.
Making chips has three steps. Design. Fabrication, in a factory called a fab. Then assembly, testing and packaging.
Fabs are among the most expensive factories on Earth. The air must be cleaner than an operating theatre, and the machines cost a fortune.

anim.title: Why it is strategic
items: A few places make most advanced chips
A shortage can stop car factories
Defence and space depend on them

segments.say: Only a few places make the most advanced chips. When supply broke during the pandemic, car factories around the world stopped.

items.text: First assembly and fab projects approved

segments.say: In December twenty twenty-one, India approved a seventy-six thousand crore rupee programme for chips and displays. Assembly plants and India's first big fab followed.
For GS Three: know the three steps, the supply risk, and India's mission to build a chip industry at home.
